approach.method_basis: The Parent is a de novo molecular optimizer that breeds graphs from a bounded score-ranked population and fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to the accepted scores of the current objective session only. Each announcement it does not simply pick ten molecules: it plans two batches at once. It forms a posterior-sampled reference batch of ten, builds thirty-two one-substitution alternatives to it, and for each candidate first batch it simulates sixteen scenarios of what those ten molecules would score, conditions the surrogate on each simulated outcome, prices an analytic policy for the batch that would follow, and keeps the first batch with the best two-batch value. Before any real label exists it also pre-generates four mutations of every molecule that could enter the first batch and reserves them as options the next decision may buy; an option becomes available because one of its generating molecules ended up in the chosen first batch, and whether that molecule survived in the breeding population no longer matters. When the real labels arrive the saved second-batch policy is executed on them, and only a purchased score ever enters the archive, the fit, the population or any reward.
approach.novelty: Those sixteen simulated first-batch scores are drawn from the surrogate's own Gaussian posterior - predicted mean plus predicted uncertainty times a standard normal. This node replaces that standard normal with the session's own track record. Every time a purchase comes back, the optimizer stores how far the real score landed from the prediction it had made for that molecule before buying it, divided by the uncertainty it had claimed. Once one announcement of such records exists, each simulated first-batch score becomes predicted mean plus predicted uncertainty times one of those stored misses, drawn uniformly, so the lookahead reasons about outcomes shaped like the ones this session has actually produced - their spread, their skew and their one-sidedness - instead of textbook Gaussian ones. The scenario stream, the dependence between the ten simulated molecules, the sixteen scenarios, the reserved option set, the policy, the physical commitment and everything the real labels feed are untouched. Earlier work on this route changed what the second decision may choose from, how exactly the saved policy is executed, and which reserved options stay available; none of them changed the distribution the valuation averages over, and the request lists no same-Parent sibling.

observed_bottleneck: On the actual code Parent n-5513a2a54383 the two-batch valuation keeps assigning positive expected gain to second batches that return none, and its own published measurement record locates the defect in the law it integrates over rather than in what it is allowed to buy. That record reports modelled second-batch gain 0.010017066634287173 against realized 0.011068338217441737, modelled-minus-realized -0.0010512715831545649, 80 of 210 committed second batches carrying strictly positive modelled recourse gain while realizing zero progress, and pooled modelled-versus-realized rank correlation -0.09325255815659536. Over its 4,350 purchases the prospective predictive-mean error is 0.020801510224934112 with MSE 0.007689199418054513 - about twice the second-batch gain the valuation prices - while only 281 of those purchases moved the incumbent at all. Each earlier repair on this route changed something other than that law and left the pattern standing: n-e68846780093 replaced the conditional policy's integration and gained 0.010053371367840994 on its own code Parent; n-59436e1eec8f aligned the valued and executed support exactly, was refuted at -0.017413267390789317, and still left 167 of 210 non-improving second batches carrying modelled recourse gain 0.007241473479038256 against realized zero; n-aedff97c8e9f added the reserved offspring bank; and the Parent then removed the bank's source-survival predicate, where 1,258 previously excluded and 971 newly eligible saved occurrences produced 22 purchases and exactly zero incumbent improvements, so its +0.0045318330800366846 endpoint gain did not run through the options it freed. The one input of that valuation never varied is the probability law of the hypothetical first-stage labels: still the inherited standard normal applied to the posterior's own moments.

adoptions.applicability: The paper's setting is a misspecified posterior whose expectations drive the decision, which is exactly this Parent's two-batch valuation on its own measured record; the correction is applied only to the one input of that valuation three previous repairs on this route left alone, and the result is read on realized two-batch progress and the endpoint rather than on coverage.

hypothesis: Replace the probability law of the hypothetical first-stage labels in the valued two-batch rollout, and nothing else. FingerprintPosterior maintains a session-local chronological store of standardized residuals - realized accepted score minus the predictive mean recorded for that purchase at its own announcement, divided by the predictive standard deviation recorded there - appended in Evolution.observe for every accepted purchase, so every stored value is prospective and real. For each of the 33 first-stage alternatives and each of the 16 outer scenarios every hypothetical label becomes mu(A) + sigma(A) * r, where sigma(A) is the Parent's own marginal predictive standard deviation of that label and r is one uniform draw from the store realized through the inherited scenario stream: the inherited Gaussian deviation is divided by sigma to expose its exactly standard-normal marginal, the normal CDF turns that into its inherited uniform rank, and the rank indexes the sorted store uniformly. The marginal law of every hypothetical label is therefore exactly the session's empirical standardized-residual law, while the scenario design and the dependence across the ten first-stage coordinates remain the inherited ones. Until the store holds one announcement of accepted purchases the inherited standard normal stands and every substitution is logged. Support, availability, the mean eligibility mask, the analytic conditional policy and its ties, the physical two-stage commitment, the one-announcement carry, the terminal immediate-only rule and every real archive, fit, retention and breeding law are unchanged; the optimization and independent evaluation rows keep the inherited standard normal; and no hypothetical label or posterior sample ever becomes an accepted label.

finding_summary.headline: The session's own residual law ran everywhere, widened the valuation gap and lost 0.0086 of endpoint
finding_summary.insights:
The route's conversion failure is not caused by the Gaussian shape of the fantasy labels. This was the one untouched input after three repairs to support, execution alignment and availability, and substituting the session's measured residual law for it made the modelled-versus-realized gap worse in both magnitude and sign while realized progress fell. That is strictly more informative than the registered split, which anticipated either a closed gap with progress or a closed gap without it: the gap did not close at all, so the campaign can now rule out miscalibration of this particular draw law as the obstacle and should stop treating the fantasy distribution as the lever.

The measured store says why, and it is the most reusable thing this node produced. The session's standardized residuals are nothing like a unit normal: across the fifteen sessions their standard deviation at the final announcement ranges from 0.60 to 22.73, skew from -4.1 to +11.1, the mean is negative in most sessions, and the extremes reach -22 and +286. Those are not the fingerprints of a well-scaled predictor with the wrong tail shape; they are the fingerprints of a predictive variance that is badly wrong in scale, sometimes far too small. Feeding that law back into the lookahead multiplies the predicted uncertainty by occasional huge misses, which inflates the best-case scenario of a second batch and raises its modelled gain - exactly the 0.0024 rise we measured - without making any real molecule better. So the diagnosis points one level up from the valuation: the limitation is the surrogate's uncertainty model itself, a session-local count-fingerprint Gaussian process with a fixed noise term fitted to a few hundred adaptively chosen points. The method that could remove it is a different predictive or ranking model - a heteroscedastic or robustly scaled noise model, or a model that is scored on how it ranks candidates rather than on its point predictions - not another law for the scenario draw and not a retuned minimum store size. The campaign's existing lesson that better calibration has never bought search value here is corroborated once more, now with a case where the calibration diagnostic itself refused to improve.

Two further method observations have measured support. First, the planning side is close to saturated: the discrete law changed the chosen first batch in 204 of 225 announcements and still moved the endpoint adversely, and exact ties among the 33 alternatives fell from 9 to 3 announcements, so the valuation is already discriminating finely among candidates that are near-equivalent in realized value. The pool it ranks, not the ranking, is where the headroom is: of 4,350 purchases only 262 moved the incumbent at all, down from 281. Second, the chemistry report shows the same ceiling from the other side. The generator builds recognizable drug-sized cores but finishes them wrongly - 22.6 percent of all proposals carry an N-halogen, O-halogen, S-halogen, peroxide or allene bond, no proposal anywhere contains a trifluoromethyl group, no stereocentre is ever specified although a quarter to nine-tenths of molecules have unassigned ones, saturated azacycles are effectively absent, and each panel wastes oracle calls on one-to-six-atom fragments. On one Objective the end of the run is halogen permutation on a single scaffold, with six molecules tied at an identical score differing only in halogen identity, which is sustained local refinement of an inherited scaffold rather than search. A proposal operator with multi-halogen groups as attachable units, carbon-directed halogenation, ring edits that close to five- and six-membered saturated heterocycles and configuration-carrying edits addresses that directly; no change to the valuation can.

What stays open: this result settles the registered label-law intervention and prices that one element negatively on this host and panel, and it does not settle whether a conformal construction with a coverage guarantee, a differently standardized residual law, or a robust predictive model would behave differently, nor does it decompose the endpoint loss into the valuation's own misvaluation versus the changed purchases, fits and populations that followed from optimizer ordinal 21 onward. Whether this approach continues is the Search Policy's call on evidence about the whole route, not a verdict this node's falsifier can deliver.
finding_summary.results:
The replacement law operated on every branch it was meant to. All fifteen sessions completed; the inherited standard normal stood only at the first announcement of each session, with its fallback logged, and from the second announcement onward every hypothetical first-batch label was the predicted mean plus the predicted uncertainty times a residual drawn from the session's own store, which grew by ten per announcement to 280 usable entries. 4,350 residuals were recorded and none skipped, none was read at or after its own announcement, and none crossed between sessions. Replaying 1,035 planning branches from the logged scenario array and the sorted store reproduced the logged labels to within 6e-17 with every discrete index matching, and with an empty store the first announcement was bitwise the code Parent's in all fifteen sessions. The law also changed real decisions: the chosen first-stage alternative differed from the Parent's in 204 of 225 announcements and the chosen first batch differed as a set in 208 of 225 announcements, and 189 of 210 committed second batches differed in identity, with divergence beginning exactly at the announcement where the store activates and the first changed purchase arriving at optimizer ordinal 21 to 44.

Every predicted consequence then went the wrong way. The modelled-minus-realized second-batch gap, which the intervention was registered to shrink below 0.00105, instead grew to 0.00217 and flipped sign: the modelled second-batch gain rose from 0.01002 to 0.01241 while the realized second-batch increment fell from 0.01107 to 0.01024, so the valuation became more optimistic rather than better matched to outcomes. Committed second batches that carried positive modelled gain and realized nothing rose from 80 to 97 of 210, and second batches realizing nothing at all rose from 104 to 119. The registered primary statistic, the equal-session mean over all 420 adjacent two-batch windows, had to rise strictly above 0.0246304; it fell to 0.0241959, which triggers the registered scientific falsifier. Within that statistic the first-batch component rose slightly, from 0.01395 to 0.01453, and the planned second-batch component fell, from 0.01107 to 0.01024, while late incumbent gains over the last half of each budget fell 42 percent, from 1.7476 to 1.0177. The surrogate's own prospective error worsened in step, from 0.0208 to 0.0230 with mean squared error 0.00769 rising to 0.00890, and the modelled-versus-realized rank correlation stayed negative, -0.093 to -0.117, with nine of fifteen sessions now negative rather than five.

The endpoint fell. Across the complete fifteen matched cells the macro mean was 0.55614 against the code Parent's 0.56479, a paired mean delta of -0.00865, four times the 0.002 margin in the adverse direction, with seeds at -0.0245, +0.0122 and -0.0137 and eight favorable against seven adverse cells; one cell, sitagliptin on seed 0, accounts for -0.1163 of it. The development target of the Parent's mean plus 0.002 was not met, and the node sits 0.0509 below the formal Anchor's published mean. The host was preserved and the added machinery was not free: only the two intended files changed, no asset or dependency was added, the scenario stream was consumed with zero additional random draws and zero additional factorizations, and announcement time rose about ten percent, 2752.5 seconds against 2494.7, with peak resident memory up about two percent.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic cores with real pharmacophores, decorated with N-halogen, O-F, S-Cl and thiol bonds; no CF3, no stereo, no azacycles
molecular.overall_character: Across the five Objectives the node proposed 4,350 optimizer molecules (870 per Objective over seeds 0/1/2, plus the same ten fixed starting molecules each session). Every one parses and sanitizes. The population is genuinely ring-rich and aromatic, consistent with the digest counters (ring_closure_rate 0.9264-0.9897, aromatic_atom_rate 0.8747-0.9782): 2.9-4.9 rings and 1.8-4.2 aromatic rings per molecule, mean molecular weight 360-591, mean SMILES length 42.9-76.4. On each Objective the high-scoring molecules converge on one recognizable medicinal-chemistry framework - an indole-2-carboxamide anilide, a purine-like fused aminopyrimidinone biaryl, an aryl/basic-amine aminergic pharmacophore, an indole-N-diketopiperazine hybrid, a fluorinated xanthine-like bicyclic - so the generator clearly can assemble drug-sized scaffolds. What it cannot do is finish them as real chemistry. 22.6% of all 4,350 proposals carry at least one N-halogen, O-halogen, S-halogen, peroxide, allene or acyl-halide bond; no proposal anywhere carries a trifluoromethyl group; charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are 0.0000 on all five panels even though 25-89% of molecules have at least one unassigned stereocentre; and saturated azacycles (piperidine, piperazine) are effectively absent while medium 8-10 membered rings are common. Each panel also contains 1.5-8.6% of one-to-six heavy-atom fragments (N, NF, ClBr, OSBr, FF, C#C) sitting at the score floor. The result is a population whose cores look like drugs and whose decorations do not. Child evaluation and Parent pairing are both complete on seeds 0/1/2, but the Parent per-molecule trajectories are not among this request trusted citation paths, so the molecule-level comparison I can make is against the Parent's own published molecular assessment: the three gaps it recorded - unconserved local functional-group environments including N-halogen attachments, absent stereochemistry, and non-conservative ring fusion and contraction - all recur here at the rates given above.

per_task.generated_character: Mid-sized aromatic amides: mean 24.3 heavy atoms, mean MW 376.6 (max 611), 3.08 rings and 2.51 aromatic rings, mean SMILES length 42.9. The dominant framework over 870 molecules is a methoxy/methyl/ethyl-substituted indole- or azaindole-2-carboxamide N-arylated with phenyl or pyridinyl; 215 of 870 share the Murcko scaffold O=C(Nc1ccccc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1 and only 265 unique scaffolds appear in total. Halogen is almost universal (digest halogen_rate 0.9345) but it is mostly on nitrogen: an N-halogen bond appears in 49.5% of the 870 molecules and 85.1% of the top-scoring decile, and 69 molecules put F, Cl or Br directly on the pyrrole-type ring nitrogen. Free thiols appear in 37.4%. No molecule carries CF3, one of 870 carries a nitrile, none carries a saturated azacycle or any formal charge, and the digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0000.
liabilities: N-chloro, N-fluoro and N-bromo amides in the highest-scoring molecules (N-halogen in 85.1% of the top decile): CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3cccnc3)n2F)c1C is an N-chloroamide bearing an N-fluoro pyrrole nitrogen, i.e. two halogenating reagents on a drug scaffold.
Halogen or sulfur placed directly on the aromatic ring nitrogen: n2F, n2Cl, n2Br in 69 molecules and n-SH in 2, as in CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3ccc(Cl)nc3)n2S)c1C at 0.4399.
Free aryl and ring thiols in 37.4% of the 870 molecules, including the second-best molecule.
Hypofluorite O-F (5 molecules) and alkyl peroxide (5 molecules), e.g. COOc1c2cc3c4cc(C(=O)N(F)c5ccccc5)n3CC(CN2)Sc14 at 0.3865.
Oracle calls spent on non-molecules: the six worst entries are N, NF, NCl, ClBr, SNBr and OSBr, which are not organic compounds at all.
Eight- and nine-membered rings formed by ring expansion in 12 molecules, e.g. COc1c2cc3c4cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c5ccccc5)n3CC(CSN2)Sc14 at 0.4064, which also contains an S-N bond in the macro-ring.
missing_features: No nitrile anywhere worth speaking of: 1 of 870 molecules carries C#N, although the best-scoring family is otherwise a close analogue of a cyanoaryl acetamide chemotype.
No tertiary N-acyl-N-alkyl aniline (tertiary acetanilide): 1.7% overall and 0% of the top 50 carry an N,N-disubstituted aniline nitrogen that is not halogenated.
No trifluoromethyl in any of the 870 molecules and a geminal difluoride in exactly one, despite 93.5% halogen content: the halogens go on singly, mostly onto nitrogen.
No saturated nitrogen heterocycle (piperidine 0.000, piperazine 0.000, saturated six-ring N 0.000).
No defined stereochemistry: 25.1% of molecules have an unassigned stereocentre and none is specified.
No ionizable centre: carboxylic acid, sulfonamide and sulfone are all 0.000-0.005 and charged_rate is 0.0000.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores run 0.0 to 0.4828 (median 0.324). The gradient rewards building the fused bicyclic heteroaromatic 2-carboxamide and switching its anilide to a pyridinyl amide (pyridine 19.5% overall, 46% of the top 50), then rewards halogen addition: top decile mean 0.418 with 25.5 heavy atoms, 3.46 rings and 85.1% N-halogen versus bottom decile mean 0.032 with 13.3 heavy atoms and 27.6% N-halogen. The clean starting molecule COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC already scores 0.3051 at evaluation 9, and the best molecule found in 300 evaluations, CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3cccnc3)n2F)c1C at 0.4828, is that same chemotype plus an N-chloro amide and a ring N-F. Six molecules tie at exactly 0.4387992465191 differing only in halogen identity and position, so the end of the run is halogen permutation on one scaffold. The score floor is occupied by fragments the optimizer made itself: N, NF, NCl, ClBr, SNBr, OSBr all at 0.0.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like population of the five: mean MW 591 (max 1622), 41.5 heavy atoms, 4.65 rings and 4.2 aromatic rings, mean SMILES length 76.4 with a maximum of 220, mean QED 0.257 and only 38% of molecules inside Lipinski limits. Two families dominate. The top family is a purine-like tetracyclic aminopyrimidinone-imidazole fused system linked to a pyrimido-pyridine bearing a sulfenyl chloride: 41 of the top 50 molecules share the single Murcko scaffold N=c1[nH]c(=O)c2cn(-c3ncnc4ncccc34)c3c2n1C3. The second family is oligomeric: benzoxazinone-aryl units repeated three or four times, which is where the 1622 Da molecule comes from. Aromatic nitrogen is everywhere (89.5% of molecules, 100% of the top 50), 230 four-membered rings and 120 nine-membered rings are present, and there is no sulfonamide, no carboxylic acid and no CF3 in any of the 870.
liabilities: Sulfenyl chloride S-Cl in 74 molecules, including every molecule in the 0.6227 tie, e.g. CN=c1n(Cl)c(=O)c2c(C)n(-c3ncnc4nc(SCl)c(C)cc34)c3c2n1C3.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The score range is compressed: worst 0.5, median 0.595, best 0.6227. Trivial molecules get half credit - O, Br, CBr, CF, CCCCC and ClCOCl all score exactly 0.5 - so the whole search operates in a 0.12-wide band. Going from 0.52 to 0.62 is paid for by fused aromatic nitrogen heterocycles and a biaryl link (top decile 40.2 heavy atoms, 4.98 rings, 4.39 aromatic rings versus bottom decile 19.3 and 2.41), and the amide and basic amine present in lower-scoring molecules disappear completely from the top decile (both 0.000). No tertiary aliphatic amine (0.2%): the basic centre is a secondary ring NH or a pendant primary CH2NH2, so the generator cannot modulate basicity or add N-alkyl groups.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The widest gradient of the five: 0.000167 to 0.9919, median 0.561. Two things pay. Mean MW 426.4, 31.2 heavy atoms, 4.94 rings, 2.61 aromatic rings, mean QED 0.604 and 85.7% of molecules inside Lipinski limits; halogen content is low (digest halogen_rate 0.1057) and 593 distinct Murcko scaffolds appear in 870 molecules, the broadest of the five. Cyclic diamide/urea motifs are in 39.2% of molecules and amides in 80.1%. The cost is strain and odd ring chemistry: 66.9% of molecules contain a bridgehead atom, 27.2% a four-membered ring, 6.7% a three-membered ring, and 580 seven- plus 315 eight-membered rings occur. 69.4% have an unassigned stereocentre and none is specified.
liabilities: Bridged and strained ring systems in the majority of molecules (66.9% bridgehead, 27.2% four-membered ring), e.g. CCOC1=C2CC2N1n1c2c3c(c1c1ccccc12)N(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C3 at 0.2081, which is a cyclopropene enol ether fused to an N-aminoindole.

An aromatic ring written with an oxygen, an NH and two nitrogens in the same five-membered ring, e.g. CCCc1ccc(OCC)c(-c2c(S)c3ccccc3o[nH]n2C2=CC(=O)CN(C)CCN(C)C2)c1 at 0.2356 - this fused o[nH]n ring is not a real heteroaromatic.
Hydrazine and N-N linkages in 13.3% of molecules, including the seed-2 endpoint CCCc1cc(NN2CCC3C(=O)NC(C)C(=O)C(=C(CC)C2)N3C)c2ccccc2n1 at 0.2086 where an aryl hydrazine replaces an aryl amine.
Ring enamines in 56.9% of molecules, giving tautomerically unstable C=C-N motifs inside the lactam rings.
Eight-membered lactam rings in 315 occurrences and a peroxide hemiketal at 0.1974 (CCCc1cc(N2CCC3C(OO)N(C)C(=O)C(=C(CC)C2)N3C)c2ccccc2n1).

No N-methylpiperazine or any saturated six-membered diamine (piperazine 0.1%, piperidine 3.1%).
No benzodioxole or other fused dioxygen ring, and no pyrazolo-fused pyrimidinone: the generator reaches the diketopiperazine half but never the fused bicyclic heteroaromatic half.

No ionizable centre (charged_rate 0.0000, carboxylic acid 0.3%).
No trifluoromethyl or aryl-CF3 group in any of the 870 molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores run 0.0 to 0.2473 (median 0.195), a narrow band that the whole run never escapes. The gradient rewards carrying two different pharmacophore halves at once: top decile amide 89.7% and 34.4 heavy atoms versus bottom decile amide 40.2% and 27.0 heavy atoms, with the cyclic N-methyl diamide and the ethoxyaryl/propyl indole both required - CCOc1ccc(C)cc1-c1c(C)c2ccccc2n1C1CC(=O)N(C)CC(=O)N(CC)C1 scores 0.2357 with both halves, while the seed-2 endpoint molecules that lose the aryl ether and keep only the diamide sit at 0.195-0.219. The best molecule of the run beats the best starting molecule (CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c(-n2cc3c(c2-c2ccccc2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C)c1 at 0.1678) by only 0.08 over 300 evaluations.

per_task.generated_character: The smallest and by far the most fluorinated panel: mean MW 360.0, 25.1 heavy atoms, 3.85 rings but only 1.8 aromatic rings, mean SMILES length 47.7. Fluorine is placed everywhere except where a chemist would put it: alkyl C-F in 61.0% of the 870 molecules, aryl C-F in 9.9%, but N-F in 14.5%, F directly on an aromatic ring nitrogen in 20.5%, and the hypofluorite O-F in 16.8% - while trifluoromethyl occurs in exactly zero molecules. The core is a 1,3-disubstituted xanthine-like pyrimidinedione or imidazo-pyrimidinedione bearing a fluorocyclobutane and a fluorinated cyclic enol-imine, e.g. the best molecule Cn1ccn(C2(F)C(F)=CN=C2O)c(C2(C)C(F)CC2F)cc(=O)n(F)c1=O at 0.6043. Small strained rings dominate: 44.8% of molecules contain a four-membered ring, 15.9% a three-membered ring, with 505 four-ring and 142 three-ring occurrences. Cyclic C=N imines appear in 22.2% and free thiols in 17.8%. 63.4% carry an unassigned stereocentre, the top 50 average 3.12 of them (up to 6), and none is specified.
liabilities: Hypofluorite O-F bonds in 146 molecules, scoring up to 0.4725: O=C(COF)C1=CC2CC1=C2n1ccn(CF)c(=O)n(CF)c(=O)cc1CF contains both an O-F bond and a bicyclo[2.1.0] diene, neither of which exists as a stable compound.
N-fluoro imide in the single best molecule, Cn1ccn(C2(F)C(F)=CN=C2O)c(C2(C)C(F)CC2F)cc(=O)n(F)c1=O - N-F on an imide nitrogen is an electrophilic fluorinating reagent, not a drug substituent.
Strained fused bicyclics in nearly half the population (44.8% four-membered, 15.9% three-membered rings), e.g. CN1CC2C(=C(C3(F)C(F)C3F)N2c2cc3c4c(S)c2OC4C3=O)C(O)N(F)C1=O at 0.4708.
Cyclic hemiaminal/enol C(O)=N and N,O-acetal motifs in 14.1% of molecules, including the top family's C(F)=CN=C2O ring.
Free thiols in 17.8% of molecules and S-F in 10, e.g. Cn1c(=O)cc(SF)n(C2=C3CC2C=C3C(=O)C(F)OF)ccn(CF)c1=O at 0.3426 which also carries a hypofluorite.
A fused 795 Da bis-xanthine oligomer proposed at score 0.0, and single-atom or diatomic fragments (F, FF) proposed repeatedly across seeds.
missing_features: No trifluoromethyl group in any of the 870 molecules - the most fluorine the generator ever gathers on one carbon is two, in 23 molecules - even though the whole gradient is about fluorine density; fluorine is otherwise added one atom at a time to whatever heteroatom is nearest.
No trifluoromethyl-substituted or trifluorinated aryl ring, the usual way to carry several fluorines on one carbon framework.
No saturated fused azacycle (piperazine 0.0%, piperidine 0.0%, saturated six-ring N 0.0%); the nitrogen-rich part is always an unsaturated or aromatic ring.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores span 1.6e-36 to 0.6043 with a median of 0.085, so the objective is multiplicative and punishing. The gradient rewards a small, compact, nitrogen- and fluorine-dense heterocycle with a carbonyl: the top decile averages 27.6 heavy atoms and 4.18 rings with N-F in 21.8% and O-F in 27.6%, while the bottom decile averages 5.0 heavy atoms and 0.52 rings at a mean score of 0.0 (F, FF, C#C at 1e-24 to 1e-26) and the 795 Da fused oligomer scores 0.0 outright. In other words both too-small and too-large are killed and the optimizer is left tuning fluorine count on a fixed small core - which it does by putting fluorine on nitrogen and oxygen, the two places it cannot go, with 146 O-F molecules scoring up to 0.4725 and the single best molecule carrying an N-F imide.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Zero of the 4,350 optimizer molecules across the five Objectives contain a trifluoromethyl or trifluoromethoxy group and only 39 (0.9%) contain any geminal dihalide - one of which is difluoromethane itself, FCF, proposed as a candidate and scored - even though four of the five panels are halogen-saturated (digest halogen_rate 0.7862-0.9736) and one panel's entire score gradient tracks fluorine density (alkyl C-F in 61.0% of its 870 molecules). Halogens arrive one atom at a time and land on whatever heteroatom is adjacent: N-halogen in up to 49.5% of a panel, F on an aromatic ring nitrogen in up to 20.5%, O-F in up to 16.8%, S-halogen in up to 8.5%.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot reliably place more than one halogen on the same carbon: no trifluoromethyl group exists anywhere in its output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Put common multi-halogen substituents into the mutation vocabulary as single attachable units (trifluoromethyl, difluoromethyl, trifluoromethoxy, geminal difluoride) so one edit can add a whole group, and make halogen-addition edits carbon-directed so a halogen cannot be attached to nitrogen, oxygen or sulfur in the first place.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over all 4,350 molecules, piperidine occurs in 0.0-3.1% per panel, piperazine in 0.0-0.8%, any saturated six-membered ring nitrogen in 0.0-3.2%, and a tertiary trialkylamine in 0.2-14.9%. On the one panel where every molecule in the top decile carries a basic ring nitrogen (97.7%), 290 of 870 molecules contain a ring of eight or more atoms and the highest-scoring molecule COc1cc(F)cc(C2=CNCCC(N(CN)c3cccc(S)c3)CNC2)c1 carries its two nitrogens in a nine-membered ring with a ring enamine; ring enamines appear in 80% of that panel's top 50.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot build ordinary saturated nitrogen heterocycles; when a basic nitrogen is needed it produces a secondary NH inside an irregular medium ring or a pendant primary amine.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add ring-construction edits that close, contract or substitute rings into five- and six-membered saturated heterocycles, an N-alkylation edit that produces tertiary amines, and a ring-size preference that keeps newly formed rings at five or six atoms unless a larger ring is explicitly intended.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0000 on all five panels and no isomeric SMILES appears in 4,350 molecules, while 25.1-89.3% of molecules per panel carry at least one unassigned stereocentre; one panel's 50 highest-scoring molecules average 3.12 unassigned centres each (up to 6) and another's average 1.34 on a 2,5-dioxopiperazine ring. Mean fraction of sp3 carbon is 0.202-0.374 and 5.3-66.9% of molecules contain a bridgehead atom, so the sp3 content that needs configuration is actually there.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never expresses stereochemistry, although most of what it proposes has stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Carry isomeric identity through every edit and add configuration-setting edits where the graph supports one, so a molecule with a real stereocentre is proposed as a defined isomer; a flat graph proposed for a stereogenic skeleton is an under-specified candidate the score cannot distinguish.

transferable_gaps.evidence: charged_rate is 0.0000 on all five panels over 4,350 molecules. Carboxylic acid is 0.000-0.003 on four panels and sulfonamide 0.000-0.002 on four; the only panel showing them at 17.8% and 18.0% inherits both from the fixed start molecules, and its top-scoring decile has dropped acid, sulfonamide and sulfone to 0.000 each. No panel ever re-attaches a sulfonyl or acid group to a core it built itself.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no ionizable chemistry: no formal charge, and acidic or sulfonyl groups it is handed are discarded rather than relocated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the edit vocabulary acidic and ionizable fragments (carboxylic acid, sulfonamide, sulfone, tetrazole, acylsulfonamide) as attachable units and allow a group removed from one position to be re-attached elsewhere, so polar decoration can be moved rather than only deleted.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each panel contains 1.5-8.6% of molecules with six or fewer heavy atoms, and the bottom of every score range is occupied by them: N, O, C, C#C, NN, NF, NCl, FF, ClBr, CBr, CF, OSBr, SNBr, ClCOCl and CCCCC all appear as proposals. One panel's lowest decile averages 5.0 heavy atoms at a mean score of exactly 0.0, and on another panel six proposals (N, NF, NCl, ClBr, SNBr, OSBr) are the six worst molecules of the run.
transferable_gaps.gap: Destructive edits are proposed as finished candidates: the generator regularly submits one-to-six heavy-atom fragments and inorganic species for scoring.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Apply a size and composition floor to edit products before they are scored - a minimum heavy-atom count, at least one ring retained, at least one carbon-carbon bond - and either repair or resample a product that falls through it, so deletion edits cannot degenerate into fragments and diatomics.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One panel has 44.8% of molecules carrying a four-membered ring and 15.9% a three-membered ring (505 and 142 ring occurrences), and the fused bicyclobutene motif C1=CC2CC1=C2, which cannot exist with that unsaturation, appears in molecules scoring up to 0.4725. Another panel reaches 66.9% bridgehead-containing molecules with 259 four-membered and 59 three-membered rings, including a cyclopropene enol ether at 0.2081, and writes a fused five-membered ring containing an aromatic oxygen next to an NH and two nitrogens (o[nH]n) at 0.2356. Medium rings of eight to ten atoms appear 290, 350 and 125 times on three panels.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring edits are gated on valence alone, so the generator produces strained and geometrically impossible frameworks and then optimizes within them.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Gate closure, contraction, expansion and fusion edits on ring strain and on whether the resulting bridged or fused system can carry its unsaturation and aromaticity, not only on whether every atom's valence is satisfied.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 22.6% of all 4,350 proposals carry at least one N-halogen, O-halogen, S-halogen, peroxide, allene or acyl-halide bond. These concentrate at the top rather than the bottom: 65% of one panel's 20 best molecules and 75% of another's carry such a bond, N-halogen rises from 27.6% in one panel's bottom decile to 85.1% in its top decile, and 74 molecules carrying a sulfenyl chloride include every molecule in a twelve-way tie at the maximum score. Alongside them sit free thiols in up to 41.5% of a panel, N,O-acetals and aminals in up to 20.9%, open-chain aldimines in 13.7% and ring enamines in up to 59.9%.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no notion of a stable local functional-group environment, so reactive and hydrolytically labile motifs accumulate exactly where the score is highest.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Score or filter edit products on local functional-group environment in addition to valence, and supply the ordinary substitute for each unstable environment the edits can create - carbon-bound halogen for N-, O- and S-bound halogen, plain amide for N-halo amide, ether or sulfone for free thiol, aminal and hemiaminal repaired to amine plus carbonyl - so a favourable core can be kept while an impossible attachment is replaced instead of inherited by every descendant.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per panel, 870 molecules span 265-593 unique Bemis-Murcko scaffolds, but the 50 highest-scoring molecules collapse to 3-28 scaffolds; on one panel 41 of the top 50 share a single scaffold and twelve molecules hit the identical score 0.6227157529678538 while differing only in peripheral substituents (propyl, butenyl, ethynyl, chloroalkyl, chloroallene, and Cl, Br or propyl on the imide nitrogen), and on another six molecules tie at 0.4387992465191 differing only in halogen identity and position. Best-so-far improved only 5-33 times per 300-observation session, and the clean tenth starting molecule of one panel (0.3051) is still the chemotype of that panel's best molecule (0.4828) 279 evaluations later.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no scaffold-level move: once a family scores well it can only permute peripheral atoms, so the end of a run re-proposes the same core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add scaffold-level edits - ring-system replacement, ring-size hop, linker exchange, core swap that preserves the substituent pattern - so a converged family can move to a different core while keeping its decoration, instead of spending the remainder of a session re-permuting peripheral atoms the score is demonstrably indifferent to.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
